prompt: An investment of $\$400$ grows by $6\%$ each year. Which expression gives the value of the investment, in dollars, after $t$ years?
hint: Growing by a *percent* each year is repeated multiplication, not repeated addition.

hints.text: Growing by a *percent* each year is repeated multiplication, not repeated addition.
Each year the value is multiplied by $1 + 0.06 = 1.06$.

learningObjective: Build an exponential growth model from a percent rate.
explanation: A $6\%$ increase means keeping the original $100\%$ and adding $6\%$ more, so multiply by $1.06$.
Choice A models linear growth of $6$ cents per year. Choice C loses $94\%$ per year. Choice D multiplies by $6$ each year.

alternativeExplanations.title: Sanity-check with one year
steps: After one year, $\$400$ growing $6\%$ should be $\$424$.
Test each choice at $t = 1$: A gives $400.06$, B gives $424$ ✓, C gives $24$, D gives $2400$.
A single well-chosen test value eliminates three choices instantly, and $t = 1$ is almost always the right one to pick.
